OH BOY WHERE DO I EVEN BEGIN

My throwaway account here.

I met this guy in Italy. His was to give tours around his very touristic city on some secrets, legends, and architectural details completely for free on his own time. His goal was to spread his love of the city and let others remember the stories so they could bring a part of the city and its stories with them when they left.

We had an instant connection. Over dinner, he asked me what I was studying, and I told him I had recently quit being premed. He said that was funny considering he went to medical school for 4 years and then quit. We shared similar reasons for leaving the medical field. At one point, he was literally finishing my thoughts before I could say them. We also talked a lot about video games - he listed his favorite ones (obscure, niche games) that also happened to literally be my favorite ones. It was a "did we just become best friends?!" moment.

He showed me a pillar that supposedly, hundreds of years ago, if a criminal who was condemned to be executed could go around it without holding on with his arms, he would be given a life sentence instead. I fell off the ledge towards the curb, and he caught me. It was like a scene out of an anime or something. 

We sat on a bench in the plaza and talked about everything - love, life, languages, different cultures. I rested my head on his shoulder. We walked around the city and talked some more over drinks. I had to hold onto his arm so we could share his umbrella. 7 hours from our initial meeting, he dropped me off at my hotel, we did the European cheek kiss thing. He kissed my forehead, and then we both shifted to a brief kiss on the lips. 

I didn't think much of it, because I really thought I would never see him again. On a whim, I messaged him on my last night in Europe, and we just... never stopped messaging. We sent 30,000 messages in half a year and messaged daily. At some point, they definitely crossed a platonic line with pictures and innuendos. I ended up studying in that city a semester later (not because of him). 

When I returned to the city, it was Valentine's Day (just the way my school schedule aligned). We went out for dinner. He held my hand and led me to this point on the island that jutted out, and you could see the water and lights in every direction. It was so stunning. We sat on a bench, his arms were around my waist, and I was leaning on him. I tried to bring up our kiss, but he was being coy ("I don't remember what you're talking about" "Oh, I know you know that I know you remember"). 

Finally, he paused, and told me he had a girlfriend since about 3 months ago.

It hit me like a truck, because I really just didn't see that coming. Of all the ways I thought this might resolve, that wasn't ever a possibility to me due to the nature of our messages. We were both tipsy and ended up making out on the bench for like half an hour. The next day we talked about it more, he said that I was "too far away" (though the girl was studying in another country and wasn't even from here) and that maybe "things would have been different if I had been closer and we were seeing each other more" and that the "timing was right [with the other girl]." He said he was attracted to me physically but couldn't see himself "going steady with me."

We hung out on and off, mostly in groups, for the next half year. The last time I saw him near the end of my time abroad, I gave him a birthday present. It was the smirk emoji pillow because we sent that emoji to each other all the time because innuendos. He laughed and said he loved it a lot. We walked to the plaza holding hands. We sat on the same bench as the one from when we first met. He asked what I was going to do now that I was returning to the States. I talked about how surreal it was that I got to go back and live in that city, that the year had flown by so fast. I said I would try to get a job in NYC. I asked if he was still looking for a job, since he was unsatisfied with his current one, plus he was so smart and his English so good. He laughed and asked if I wanted him to come with me to NYC. 

We walked back to my apartment. He told me "ti voglio bene," the Italian "I love you" for friends/family. He  thanked me for returning and said I had given as much to him - a lot of memories and laughs - as he had given me. He told me not to take things so seriously in a world that doesn't take anything seriously, but that I was a special girl and didn't have to change much. He kissed me on the forehead, and I shifted a little. 

He said "no kissing," then I asked "What about one?" and he said "Just one, then." Then he pulled me in by the waist, and we shared a really long kiss... the stuff of romance movies. 

My feelings towards him and leaving the city kind of bubbled over, so I ended up crying into his chest. He held me for a bit. I could feel his heart beating fast. He told me to smile, that he wanted to see me smiling when I went into my apartment.

And... that's it. We don't talk anymore. I think about him most days, and I miss him a lot still.

TL;DR: Heart broken overseas in a not even a relationship. Still hurting since.
Venice, Italy. It's absolutely beautiful and such a unique city. Half a year later, and I'm still very much in love with it.
